pages.text: Older QMD releases exposed accelerators as the OpenComputers component $(l)component.qmd_accelerator$(). That optional ABI and its OC peripherals are not reintroduced. These pages retain the old command names as a migration reference for server-side scripts.

The Accelerator Computer Port now exposes two common server-side methods with no scripting-mod dependency: $(l)computerSnapshot()$() reads machine state and $(l)computerSetPercentage(int)$() controls output. A server integration can call these methods directly.

pages.title: Accelerator Control
pages.text: $(l:multiblocks/open_computers/oc_commands#set_energy_percentage)computerSetPercentage(int)$(/l) is the supported control operation. $(l:multiblocks/open_computers/oc_commands#snapshot)computerSnapshot()$(/l) returns a CompoundTag containing a consistent copy of the accelerator's synchronized state.

The percentage accepts every value from -1 through 100. A value of -1 selects redstone control; 0 stops accelerator output; values from 1 through 100 select the requested operating percentage. Invalid values and calls on an unavailable or unassembled machine return false.

Calls must target an Accelerator Computer Port on the logical server. Snapshot data is read-only input to the script; changing the returned tag does not change the machine. Beam-port switching and the old computer-control toggle have no replacement in this common API.
